newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products see gas oil remaining firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products see gas oil remaining firm.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices were mixed with fuel oil and light distillates slipping on softer crudes while gas oil and kerosene maintained their strength.

Traders said gas oil prices were propped by Chinese buying. China was said to have bought up to 90,000 tonnes around $199.50 a tonne c+f southern China for prompt lifting. China continued to seek gas oil around $195-$196, over their threshold price of $192-$195. On Monday a European major sold 30,000 tonnes of prompt gas oil to a Singapore trader at 68 cents a barrel over Singapore quotes fob. The major was expected to win Taiwan's sale tender over $25.50 for end-September lifting fob.

Bids on Tuesday was seen up to $25.50 a barrel for two cargoes of 200,000-220,000 barrels for mid and late September lifting, up from $25.30 on Monday. An offer for late September was seen at 50 cents a barrel over Singapore quotes fob. A major bid for 120,000 barrels of jet fuel at $28.80 for late September lifting, 10 cents over the deal done Monday between a Singapore trader and a European major. A US trader also sold Monday 100,000 barrels to a Dutch trader at a 10-cent premium fob.
Naphtha fell with lower crudes but Singapore premiums were steady around 55 cents on talk that a refiner sold 120,000 barrels for second-half September around that premium fob basis.

Paper levels dipped with September talked at $19.45-19.55. Gasoline was unchanged on talks of further exports from this region to Africa and the West. Sources also report of a Yanbu cargo fixed to Africa. Prices are expected to hold steady at about $21.50 as excess products are taken.

A local trader said he would be willing to sell September-loading barrels at $104.50 a tonne fob Singapore. The trader said demand remained soft as Singapore supplies have to compete with S.Korean sellers for sale outlets. Traders said Chinese demand were seen but bids were weak at $108 per tonne for delivery to southern China.--SINGAPORE NEWSROOM(+65-8703084)
